title: New Year’s Eve at home with a private chef: how to plan the night
summary: Plan a New Year's Eve dinner at home with a private chef: menu style, timings, drinks, real costs and two real NYE dinners from yhangry chefs.
body_markdown:
New Year’s Eve at home has a lot going for it. No surge-priced set menu, no queue for a taxi at 12:15, and nobody has to leave just as the night gets going. The trick is deciding what kind of evening you want before you think about food. Is it a long, slow dinner that rolls into the countdown, or an earlier meal and then drinks and music?


Tell your chef which one you’re picturing and ask what timings are realistic. Booking dinner doesn’t automatically mean the chef will still be there at midnight, so it’s worth agreeing that up front.


## Choose a meal that fits the night


A plated dinner gives the evening shape: everyone sits down together and each course lands at once. Sharing dishes keep things looser, so people talk, pass plates and help themselves. Canapés or a[standing, cocktail-party format](https://yhangry.com/blog-host-an-amazing-cocktail-party/) can work for a bigger crowd, but say whether the food is replacing dinner or just keeping people going between drinks.


Be honest about your space, too. The number of people who can stand in your living room isn’t the number who can sit and eat comfortably. Talk through table space,[what the chef will need in the kitchen](https://yhangry.com/blog/private-chef-kitchen-requirements/) and whether you’ll need an extra pair of hands for service when you discuss the menu. Our guide to[what’s included when you hire a private chef](https://yhangry.com/blog/whats-included-when-you-hire-a-private-chef/) covers what’s usually part of the booking.


## Two real New Year’s Eve dinners


**A plated dinner for a big group in Balham.** For New Year’s Eve 2024, a host in south London asked for a three-course sit-down dinner that felt a bit special, with a cocktail-party feel and one vegetarian at the table.[Chef Georgi](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/georgi-v/) cooked:


Booked for 14 guests, it came to £1,414.40, or about £101 a head. The host gave it five stars and singled out how clearly Georgi communicated his arrival and serving times beforehand. He also added a round of canapés and a palate cleanser between courses, and the kitchen was spotless when he left.


**A relaxed feast in a rented house in the Forest of Dean.**


A year later, a group of 16 at a holiday rental wanted the opposite: a casual, buffet-style dinner party with several different diets to cater for.[Chef James](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/james-l/) built a sharing spread that started with baked camembert with honey and walnuts, a board of Italian meats, and a wild mushroom, miso and cashew parfait. Mains were slow-baked lamb shoulder with pomegranate couscous, baked salmon with glass noodles and black bean chilli sauce, and a vegan beetroot, spinach and mushroom Wellington. Pudding was a choice of vegan Basque cheesecake, chocolate brownie with salted caramel miso sauce, or orange blossom pavlova, with a cheese board to finish (plus a separate vegan one).


It came to £1,250, roughly £78 a head. The host said the menu suited everyone’s dietary needs, that James worked happily with the rental kitchen, and that there was plenty left for New Year’s Day. If you like the sound of his cooking, James talks about foraging, fermenting and[why he chose private dining over catering](https://yhangry.com/chef-james-why-i-chose-private-dining-over-catering/) .


Both are past bookings rather than quotes. Your date, location, group and menu will set your own price.


## What New Year’s Eve dinners cost


Across 299 New Year’s Eve dinners booked through yhangry in the UK over the last three years (31 December 2023, 2024 and 2025), the typical booking came to £936. Half fell between £651 and £1,248. The usual group was about 10 people, and the typical cost worked out at around £104 a head. That covers the chef, ingredients, cooking, serving and clean-up, so budget separately for drinks.


## Agree the timings in writing


Set a guest arrival time, a time you’d like to eat and an agreed finish for the chef. If you want food later in the evening, put it in the brief now rather than asking during dessert.


Tell the chef about any toast, surprise or plan to head outside for fireworks. A five-minute pause is easy to work around; a 40-minute one can ruin a course that’s already cooking. Plenty of chefs plan their whole evening around timings like this.[Chef Mbark explains how he runs an event to the minute](https://yhangry.com/chef-mbark-time-management-yhangry/) .


## Give drinks their own plan


Decide who’s buying and serving drinks, including the alcohol-free options. Do you need extra glasses or ice? Is anyone pouring? A chef plating three courses for 14 can’t run a bar at the same time, so if you want drinks service, ask whether extra staff can be added to the booking.


Clear fridge space for the chef’s ingredients before you stock up on bottles, and keep the route between the kitchen and the table clear. Guests wander on New Year’s Eve.


## Book early and check the terms


New Year’s Eve is one of the busiest nights of the year for private chefs. Across those 299 bookings, hosts typically confirmed their chef about five weeks before the night, and half confirmed somewhere between two and nine weeks ahead. (That’s from confirmed payment to the dinner itself, so the first enquiry usually comes earlier.)

Before you pay, check the payment terms, cancellation policy, how long the chef will stay and any date-specific charges. Ask when your final guest numbers and menu need to be locked in, and keep the agreed total and what it includes in your booking conversation. If your first-choice chef is already booked, ask what the alternatives actually are rather than assuming someone else will cook the same menu to the same timings.


## Plan the last hour


Decide what happens once the meal is over. Agree clean-up and departure with the chef, and pick one guest as the go-to person for any practical questions, so it isn’t you all night. If you’d like a late snack around midnight, ask the chef to plan and leave something properly rather than relying on leftovers from dinner. If you’re hosting in a holiday house, our[holiday cottage checklist](https://yhangry.com/blog/private-chef-holiday-cottage-checklist/) covers the practical bits.

Frequently asked questions


How much does a private chef cost on New Year's Eve?


The typical UK New Year’s Eve booking on yhangry has come to about £936, with half between £651 and £1,248. Per head, that’s usually around £104, a little less for bigger groups.


Will the chef stay until midnight?


Not automatically. The booking covers the meal service you agree, so if you want the chef or staff there for the countdown, say so in your request and confirm it before you pay.


How far ahead should I book?


As early as you can. Hosts typically confirm their New Year’s Eve chef about five weeks before, and the most popular chefs fill up first.


Can the chef cater for different diets on the night?


Yes. Both dinners above handled vegetarian or vegan guests within the main menu, so nobody ended up with a separate plate. List every allergy and diet in your request and double-check it before the day.
